headline: Deploy {arm:atlas-m}. It satisfies all eleven quality, safety, and latency gates across every task.
lede: {arm:atlas-m} is the only evaluated candidate that clears every quality threshold while remaining within the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget. Relaxing the latency ceiling would allow {arm:atlas-l}, which achieves higher overall quality but exceeds p95 limits.

slots.text: Adopt {arm:atlas-m}. It clears all quality and behavioral gates across all five tasks while staying under the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency ceiling.
{arm:atlas-l} breaches the p95 latency ceiling on multiple tasks, while {arm:brisk-s} and {arm:open-70b} fail core quality and safety gates.

Watch {weakest.arm}'s {weakest.criterion} in Troubleshooting (multi-turn), which hit {weakest.value} against the {weakest.threshold} threshold with a margin of {weakest.margin} points. Multi-turn troubleshooting volume needs continuous monitoring.
Run an expanded sample of multi-turn troubleshooting cases on {arm:atlas-m} to confirm resolution rates remain securely above {criteria.trouble.resolves.threshold}.

method.text: Benchmarked four candidate models across five representative concierge task suites encompassing {scoreboard.atlas-m.cases} total cases.
All candidates had to satisfy the {criteria.overall.threshold}% Overall quality floor and {criteria.p95.threshold} Latency budget (p95) on every task, plus task-specific safety bars.
Overall quality evaluated with a calibrated judge with {judged.overall.agreement} agreement against human raters across {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} calibration pairs.
Measured end to end from incoming user message to final token completion in staging environments.
